title: The Delegation Divide: An Open Index of AI-Agent Delegability across Occupations and Countries
abstract: arXiv:2610.30752v1 Announce Type: new  Abstract: 35.2% of task time in world employment is at least partly delegable to AI agents in 2026, and only 2.5% can be handed over in full. Existing measures score exposure to generative AI, mostly for the United States. We build the Agent Delegability Index (ADI): two language models rate all 18,796 O*NET 30.2 task statements on a frozen, preregistered rubric of delegation levels and barriers; tasks are mapped to 433 ISCO-08 unit groups and weighted by ILOSTAT employment in 146 countries. Four findings. First, delegable employment rises with income, from 22.5% in low-income to 48.7% in high-income countries, a slope of 7.23 percentage points per log point of GDP per capita. This delegation divide is compositional: the physical barrier dominates the jobs poorer countries employ most. Second, at the occupation level ADI tracks exposure closely (r = 0.93 with Eloundou et al. and 0.89 with Felten et al.), above the preregistered bound of 0.80; ADI

translated_title: 委托鸿沟：一个跨职业与跨国家的AI智能体可委托性开放指数
translated_abstract: 2026年，全球就业中35.2%的任务时间至少可以部分委托给AI智能体，而只有2.5%的任务可以完全交由AI处理。现有的衡量指标主要评估对生成式AI的暴露程度，且大多仅针对美国。我们构建了智能体可委托性指数：由两个语言模型依据预先注册且冻结的委托水平与障碍评分标准，对O*NET 30.2中的全部18,796条任务陈述进行评级；再将任务映射到433个ISCO-08职业单位组，并以146个国家的ILOSTAT就业数据进行加权。研究得出四项发现。第一，可委托的就业比例随收入水平上升，从低收入国家的22.5%升至高收入国家的48.7%，斜率为人均GDP每增加一个对数点对应7.23个百分点。这一“委托鸿沟”是构成性的：物理障碍在较贫穷国家就业最集中的职业中占据主导地位。第二，在职业层面，ADI与暴露度指标高度吻合（与Eloundou等人的相关性r=0.93，与Felten等人的相关性为0.89），高于预先注册设定的0.80界值；ADI
tldr: 该研究构建了首个覆盖146个国家的AI智能体可委托性指数（ADI），发现2026年全球35.2%的就业任务时间可至少部分委托给AI智能体、仅2.5%可完全委托，且可委托比例随国家收入水平显著上升，揭示了主要由物理障碍造成的“委托鸿沟”。
en_tdlr: This study introduces the Agent Delegability Index (ADI), finding that in 2026, 35.2% of global task time is at least partly delegable to AI agents (only 2.5% fully delegable), and delegability rises steeply with national income—a "delegation divide" driven mainly by physical barriers in poorer countries.
